name: German Hefeweizen
title: German Hefeweizen: Style Guide | Craft Beer School
desc: Hefeweizen explained: Bavarian wheat beer with banana, clove and a cloudy pour, how the yeast makes it, and what Indian food to pair it with.
tagline: Cloudy, fizzy Bavarian wheat beer where the yeast does the talking: banana, clove and fresh bread.
tastes:
Hefe means yeast and weizen means wheat, which describes the beer exactly. At least half the grist is wheat malt, and the beer is served with its yeast, so it pours cloudy with a tall white head. All the fruit and spice comes from a special Bavarian yeast strain, not from anything added.

That yeast makes isoamyl acetate, which smells of banana, and 4-vinyl guaiacol, which smells of clove. The brewer steers the balance with fermentation temperature and pitching rate: warmer and lighter on yeast pushes banana, cooler pushes clove. A good one has both, with a soft bread note from the wheat and almost no hop bitterness.

Bavarians drink it at lunch, with white sausage and pretzels, and it is one of the most consistent styles in the world. It also has a short shelf life. Those delicate esters fade after a few weeks, so fresh really is best.

profile.look: Pale straw to gold, cloudy with yeast, and a tall, dense, long lasting white head.
profile.aroma_flavour: Banana and clove from the yeast, sometimes vanilla or bubblegum, over soft bread and light lemon. Hops barely noticeable.
profile.mouthfeel: Medium light body, creamy and fluffy, high carbonation, a soft and slightly tart finish.
profile.ingredients: Fifty to seventy per cent wheat malt with pilsner malt. Small amounts of noble German hops. A Bavarian weizen yeast is essential, and some brewers still use a decoction mash.

in_india: Hefeweizen is the beer most Indian brewpubs open with, and it is easy to see why. It is low in bitterness, soft, cold and fruity, and it handles 35 °C afternoons well. Ask for it fresh on tap rather than a bottle that has sat in a warm shop, because the banana and clove fade fast in the heat. Swirl the last few centimetres in the bottle and pour the yeast in; that cloudiness is part of the style.

pairings.why: Soft wheat and banana esters suit the mild, creamy tomato gravy, and the bubbles cut the butter.
The clove note picks up the garlic chutney, and the fizz deals with the fried batter.
Coconut milk, whole spice and flaky layers match the beer's soft body and gentle spice.
Semolina, ghee and ripe banana line up with the yeast's banana character.
